name: ambilight-paints-the-near-edge
description:
End to end and in pixels: the sidebar carries the colour of the page edge BESIDE it, and the whole chain from surface copy to painted glow is what makes that true.

The two fixtures are mirrors - crimson-left/blue-right and blue-left/crimson-right. Their whole-frame averages are IDENTICAL, so a sampler that averaged the frame, or a painter that laid one flat wash, reads the same on both and this scenario measures zero. Only a reader that takes the left edge specifically, handing it to a painter that puts it on the left, can move these pixels.

This is the assertion that joins the two halves proved separately elsewhere: AtriumEdgeTintTest paints a known tint, ambilight-reads-both-edges samples a known page, and neither one observes the seam between them.

actions.note: let the crimson-left page commit and paint, so there is a surface to copy

the mirrored page committed, read from the page itself

assertions.label: the-switch-really-happened
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the mirrored page committed, so the measurement below is not two captures of the same page.

assertions.label: the-sampler-saw-the-mirror
assertions.desc: The sampler read the mirrored page the other way round. Named exactly, because the whole scenario rests on left and right not being interchangeable.

THE MEASUREMENT: the sidebar backdrop followed the page's LEFT edge from crimson to blue. Both pages carry the same average colour, so nothing but a left-edge read painted on the left can move this region.
assertions.note: The band the glow paints: 32 DIP out from the card's left edge at about x=225 in the VM frame, at 55 percent of the glass alpha. Re-measured 2026-08-27 when the glow was narrowed and dimmed.
